source.title: InversionView: A General-Purpose Method for Reading Information from Neural Activations
source.authors: Xin-Ting Huang; Madhur Panwar; Navin Goyal; Michael Hahn

record.tranche_reason: The study applies InversionView, a different method from the original circuit analyses, to read information from GPT-2 small IOI head activations and compares the interpretations with Wang et al.'s findings. It does not rerun the original circuit faithfulness, completeness, or minimality tests.
record.gate_note: The IOI results in Table 2 report interpretations of individual head outputs and are recorded below. The DLA comparison in Table 4 reports rates for whether names appear among promoted or suppressed tokens, but it tests DLA's readout of heads rather than the circuit's roles or behavior; it is not used as a claim-version row. The paper's separate character-counting, addition, and factual-recall findings do not bear on these IOI versions.
record.test_reason: InversionView, a different method from Wang et al.'s patching, reads what each of the 26 IOI-circuit heads in GPT-2 small encodes. Table 2 checks each against Wang et al.'s stated role. This bears on V1's head roles but not its faithfulness, completeness or minimality criteria. No head is ablated, so V2 is not tested. Results are not split by template, so V6 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say InversionView's readouts of the IOI heads agree highly with Wang et al. and differ in only 3 of 26 heads (0.1, 0.10, 5.9). They add that these 3 were challenging for the earlier methods, which lacked direct evidence on what those heads move. They present this as simplifying interpretation and as showing InversionView scales to larger models.
record.recipe_differences: Applies InversionView's activation-conditioned input generation and cosine-distance ϵ-preimages to components already identified in the IOI circuit, rather than reproducing the original circuit-discovery and causal-validation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: For IOI, the authors report that cosine distance with ϵ = 0.1 gives convenient interpretations. Normalized Euclidean distance gives similar interpretations at a higher threshold, such as ϵ = 0.4; at ϵ = 0.1, some query activations yield few or no in-preimage samples.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct logit attribution fails to expose the S name for heads not directly connected to the output: 0% for most heads, best 7.5% for 8.10, 98.8% for 9.9 (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Readout of IOI head roles depends on the interpretation method: DLA recovers only direct-effect heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Name mover 9.9's output resembles its IOI 'to' activation at other positions, e.g. after 'gave' and at the period, i.e. name copying outside the IOI prediction slot (Appendix A.3, Figure 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI name-mover heads perform general name copying beyond the IOI slot.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine distance at ϵ=0.1 and normalized Euclidean distance at ϵ=0.4 give the same head interpretations (Appendix E.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpretations of IOI head content are robust to the choice of distance metric.

record.problems: The IOI decoder's reported average in-preimage rate is 58.0%. Interpretations are qualitative and not reported separately by template. The study does not causally validate these IOI head roles with its own patching experiments or test the circuit-level faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant IOI head-interpretation rows were left out. Table 4's DLA rates were excluded because they test a readout method's ability to expose head information, not the circuit roles or IOI behavior specified by the versions.

untested.parts: Faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the 26-head circuit. No knockout or patching of the IOI circuit is run in this study. Only per-head information content is examined.
No ablation of name-mover heads. Backup heads' IO content in clean runs (R18–R20) says nothing about takeover.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints or task reuse of IOI components.
No alternative circuit-discovery method, ablation type or metric is used to recover the circuit.
No faithfulness or completeness measurement under different ablations, metrics or distributions.

BABA and ABBA templates are mixed in decoder data, and results are not reported per template, name order or more names. Table 2 does note that head 2.2 sometimes attends to 'and' when S1 follows IO, a template-dependent behaviour, but this is not a test.

missing.what: S-Inhibition head 8.6 at END: 'Position of S1 (relative position to IO)', judged consistent with Wang et al.; grouped with 7.3

record.verdict_notes: The study's goal is validating InversionView; the IOI analysis is a qualitative per-head comparison, with no causal verification of the IOI circuit. The decoder's average in-preimage rate is 58.0%. For 5.9 the authors do not claim a contradiction, only that the role is invisible in an IOI-only input space, so no verdict is given on it. The original source is Wang et al.; this study is not an original.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not knock out everything outside the circuit or test the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. Its head-role evidence is an activation-content interpretation, not a causal test of all stated roles under patching.
The study does not ablate main name-mover heads and test whether backup heads take over.
No other model, size, checkpoint, or task reuse of the IOI circuit is tested.
The study does not compare circuit-finding methods or ablation types for recovery of the circuit. It compares activation-distance metrics for InversionView, not circuit discovery.

The study does not measure how circuit faithfulness or completeness changes across ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions. Its distance-metric discussion concerns interpretation of head activations.

The decoder training data includes BABA and ABBA templates, and interpretations are reported as consistent across query inputs, but results are not separately reported by template or name order. More than two names and other prompt formats are not tested.
